Smart Real-Time Monitoring & Inspection Mobile App for DoSJE
Smart India Hackathon 2026
The Smart India Hackathon 2026 problem statement SIH26095 addresses a critical governance gap in the Ministry
of Social Justice & Empowerment's (MoSJE) scheme implementation ecosystem. The Department of Social Justice
and Empowerment (DoSJE) runs dozens of welfare schemes through thousands of NGOs, institutions, and project
centres across India, but current monitoring mechanisms remain periodic, manual, and heavily dependent on self-
reported data from implementing agencies.
Recent CAG audits have exposed severe monitoring failures: in Maharashtra alone, six "ghost hostels" received ₹1.62
crore over four years despite housing zero students, and a December 2025 CAG report on PMKVY found 94.53% of
beneﬁciary records had missing or bogus bank details. Rajasthan's 2026 NMMS audit detected 2.56 lakh duplicate
face-authentication photographs in MGNREGA attendance, with 2.05 lakh cases from Jaisalmer district alone.
While India has deployed multiple digital monitoring systems (NMMS, AwaasSo�, RuralOne, GIA Inspection App,
MoSJE Uniﬁed Portal), signiﬁcant gaps remain: no real-time CCTV integration, no AI-based anomaly detection, no
randomised surprise inspection assignment, and no cross-veriﬁcation between attendance, location, and
beneﬁciary presence. SIH26095 seeks to address these gaps through a centralized mobile application enabling live
CCTV feeds, random video conferencing, geo-tagged inspections, and AI-driven analytics.
This report provides 16 sections of evidence-based research to support your SIH PPT, including real-world problem
documentation, existing systems analysis, international benchmarks, legal/privacy context, 15+ research papers,

Real-time monitoring in this context means:
Live CCTV video feeds from institution premises accessible to DoSJE oﬃcials without visiting

Random video conferencing with staﬀ/beneﬁciaries to conﬁrm presence and functioning

Surprise inspections are unannounced physical or virtual visits where:
NGO/institution receives no advance notice — cannot prepare fake records or stage beneﬁciaries
Inspectors arrive randomly — not on ﬁxed schedules
Video calls can be initiated unexpectedly to verify staﬀ/beneﬁciary presence

Proxy functioning occurs when:
An institution appears operational on paper but is actually closed or minimally functional
Staﬀ marked as present are absent — someone else signs attendance

Services are not actually delivered — funds are taken but no training, no rehabilitation, no education occurs

Title: 5 Evidence-Backed Innovation Pillars
Content:
1. Multi-Source Veriﬁcation (Presence Score 0-100): Combine face + liveness + GPS + CCTV cross-check + historical
consistency. Research: legitimate users ~92/100, GPS spooﬁng ~38/100.
2. AI-Assisted Risk-Based Prioritization: Hybrid rule-based + ML anomaly detection. Rules catch obvious fraud
("31st February"); ML catches subtle patterns. Research: 97%+ AUC achievable.
3. Randomised Surprise Inspections: Time-window randomisation + inspector-institution random matching +
risk-weighted probability. Unpredictable, fair, eﬃcient.
4. Privacy-Preserving CCTV Analytics: Edge processing (video on-device, metadata only to server) + privacy
masking (blur faces) + purpose-limited feeds (common areas only) + 30-day auto-deletion. DPDP-compliant.
5. Cross-Scheme Uniﬁed NGO Proﬁle: All schemes, inspections, anomalies, feedback in one view. Cross-scheme
risk scoring. Consolidated inspections reduce burden.
